name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.130.0 — The host testCommand and gateCommand now carry --test-timeout=45000 --test-force-exit so a test that opens a socket and never resolves is a bounded 45-second red instead of an unbounded hang; the file-budget reporter's own destination moves from stdout to stderr because a second reporter sharing stdout loses its tail under force-exit. A new deterministic /spec:doctor check 18, port-check.js, walks every file under tests/ and reports any fixed listen() literal, pid- or random-derived computed port, or --port <n> literal so the class of window spec 06 removed cannot creep back in; it is advisory and names no host-specific remedy path. 7.129.0 — Serve-backed tests no longer choose port numbers: design-atlas.js serve --port 0 binds an ephemeral port and announces the bound one, and tests/helpers.js now exports one shared freePort()/serveAtlas() pair that every serve-backed test harness goes through. 7.128.0 — CLIENT replaces SIGNOFF as the last human gate of /spec:mocks: the driver derives CLIENT where it derived SIGNOFF, `client open --address <url>` records an exposed serve after probing `<url>/client/__notes/list` over http or https, and design-atlas.js serve grows a /client route whose writes stamp a note's origin from the route it arrived on rather than the typed name. A client's mock-scope note captures its anchored screen at raise through lib/client-capture.js (the look command's own URL form and first-declared viewport, sha256 on the note); `notes address --port <n>` re-captures and refuses an unchanged hash, so a fix is recorded only on a visible change. Only the client route resolves a client note — withdrawn from open, accepted from addressed — and a session-route resolve is a 403. `notes waive --id --reason` releases a client note or a question after seven days of client silence, marking a question's ledger row `waived <date>`, and `--mark approved` prints the waived count and every reason. writeNotes becomes a tmp-file rename so two writers can never tear notes.json.
